title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial 'tame topology' (topologie modérée), here in the 1-dimensional case. There is a totally ordered set I. 'Structures' consist of strata M = M_0 ∪ M_1: 0-strata are points, and 1-strata are intervals X = [a,b] with boundary ∂X = {a,b}. 'Figures' are finite ≤-closed sets of strata. In an earlier text, 'CF III', he worked under a hypothesis on I: I was a 'tronçon adonné', with tame ('modérées') and constructible subsets.

The page proposes dropping that hypothesis. One must then allow 1-strata X = [a,b] with a<b and ]a,b[ = ∅, i.e. consecutive elements of a discretely ordered I. For such X it would be unreasonable to set supp X = [a,b]; the support should collapse to supp ∂X = {a,b}.

The remedy is to make the support relative to a finite totally ordered subset Δ = {a_1 < … < a_n} ⊂ I. Normally Δ = ∪_α ∂X_α. Take the Boolean algebra generated by the abstract 'points'
 {a_1}, ]a_1,a_2[, {a_2}, ]a_2,a_3[, …, {a_n}.
In the manuscript the open intervals are written with closed brackets. These atoms are the cells of the cell decomposition of I cut out by Δ. They are formal: an open-interval atom is kept even when it is set-theoretically empty in I.

For any family 𝒳 = {X_α} ⊂ M subordinate to Δ (∂X_α ⊂ Δ for all α), supp 𝒳 is defined as a subset of this finite set of atoms. Order relations are then defined 'virtually':
- X < Y when Y ≪ X (refinement);
- hence F < G for F ≤ G, for figures in the ≤-closed part of ℱ generated by 𝒳.

The page ends by remarking that this only means: for every figure in a 'scale' (échelle), drawn as a subdivided segment a_1, a_2, …, a_n, one has a Boolean algebra of 'tame parts' adapted to it.

The next page turns this into the notion of 'réalisation par rapports' of a structure in a set P of points. These are compatible maps φ*: P(F̃) → P(F̃') for refinements F' ≪ F, i.e. a Boolean-algebra / point-free realization of the combinatorial stratified structure.

Purpose: make tame topology on an ordered line independent of density or completeness assumptions. Support becomes a formal, combinatorially defined Boolean object attached to a finite subdivision, rather than a subset of I.
errors: The list of atoms writes [a_1,a_2], [a_2,a_3] with closed brackets. To give disjoint atoms of a Boolean algebra these must be the open intervals ]a_i,a_{i+1}[; this is a notational slip (or a transcription ambiguity).

The definition of supp 𝒳 and of the 'virtual' order relations is sketched elliptically. It is not checked that the support is independent of the choice of Δ (compatibility under enlarging Δ). The next page shows he recognizes this as the real issue (refinements and pre-compatibility).

ideas.what: Tame topology on a totally ordered set without density hypotheses, allowing degenerate 1-cells [a,b] with empty interior, whose support is just {a,b}
ideas.modern_name: o-minimal / cell-decomposition framework on arbitrary (including discrete) linear orders; finite unions of points and intervals
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries; Pillay–Steinhorn and Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimality, 1984–86); Grothendieck's call for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology in general terms, not this 1-dimensional formalism

ideas.what: Support of a family of strata as a subset of the finite set of atoms (points and open intervals) cut out by a finite set Δ of endpoints, i.e. elements of the Boolean algebra generated by these atoms
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra of a cell decomposition / face poset; constructible sets relative to a stratification

ideas.what: Defining order relations 'virtually' (X<Y for Y≪X) on figures to compare refinements, leading on the next page to 'realization by rapports' of a structure in a point set P (point-free/Boolean realization compatible with subdivision)
ideas.modern_name: geometric realization of a stratified combinatorial structure via a direct system of finite Boolean algebras (Stone duality, limits over subdivisions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related to Stone duality and to combinatorial models of tame spaces

missed.claim: An attempt to make the support/realization of tame (1-dimensional) stratified structures purely combinatorial and Boolean, with formal cells that may be empty, independent of hypotheses on the underlying order. It remains a sketch, part of Grothendieck's broader unfinished axiomatic tame-topology program.
missed.quote: Mais on doit pouvoir définir une notion de support, associé à une partie tot. adonnée quelconque Δ de I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a point-free approach to o-minimal / tame structures over arbitrary orders. It may relate to definable-set Boolean algebras and spectral spaces of o-minimal structures (Pillay, Coste–Roy, Edmundo). It is of modest historical interest as evidence of Grothendieck's independent 1986 approach, contemporaneous with o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful foundational bookkeeping for a 1-dimensional tame topology. The handling of discrete orders and formal cells is natural and close to standard o-minimal / cell-decomposition thinking. It is of historical interest as part of the unpublished Analysis situs, but contains no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: '(genre "triangles admissibles"[?])' should read '(genre "tronçons adonnés")', referring back to the hypothesis on I in CF III.
'Je pense qu'on ... = une bonne formulation' is likely 'Je pense qu'on [peut trouver] une bonne formulation sans hyp. sur I'.
'support, gardant[?] à une partie tot. ordonnée[?] quelconque' is more plausibly 'support, associé à une partie tot. adonnée quelconque Δ de I' (cf. 'totalement adonnée' on p.70).
'au lieu de = [-...-] supp ∂X' reads 'au lieu de supp ∂X', with a crossed-out word.
The atoms [a_1,a_2], [a_2,a_3] should be understood as open intervals ]a_i,a_{i+1}[.
'on définit ... virtuelle[?] X<Y pour Y≪X, d'une définition ... F<G' reads roughly 'on définit virtuellement X<Y pour Y≪X, d'où une définition [virtuelle] F<G pour F≤G'.
'partie ≤-fermée de F engendrée par 𝒳' has a script ℱ (the set of figures), not F.
